sentence_stem: Had the committee listened to the experts,
correct_completion: the policy would have failed far less badly.
full_sentence: Had the committee listened to the experts, the policy would have failed far less badly.
acceptable_variants: the policy would have been more successful.
the costly mistakes would have been avoided.

options.text: the policy would fail far less badly now.
options.why_wrong: The stem refers to a past unreal condition, so the result needs 'would have' plus past participle. 'Now' conflicts with the past reference.

options.text: the policy failed because of the experts.
options.why_wrong: This is a real past event with a cause. It does not complete the hypothetical result introduced by the inverted 'Had'.

options.text: the policy has been failing for years.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect continuous describes a real ongoing situation. It does not express the unreal result of the condition.

options.text: the policy would have failed far less badly.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with inverted 'had' in the if-clause
explanation: The inverted form Had the committee listened replaces If the committee had listened. The main clause must use would have plus a past participle to express an unreal past result.
translation: Se o comitê tivesse ouvido os especialistas, a política teria fracassado de forma bem menos grave.
